answer: A cliff semaphore blocks batch keys. A key bonds 1.73 POA for one 17-hour mast and posts a 19-byte pennant hash. It must flash six raven bursts, each a 17-byte signal signed 63 minutes apart from a fresh /19, then collect a return echo from two relays under 920 ms, bound to the pennant and live tip. Four clerks replay every burst and void a reused /16 or two bursts closer than 55 minutes. If five masts light under one wallet in 9 hours, or two pennants share three prefixes, all go dark and the stake is sunk. A missed burst or late echo leaves the mast unlicensed; no second mast is issued.
